No open issue shares the mechanism.

Reproduced on pristine by the classifier with the finder's repro.sql unchanged; deterministic (dblink commit, no timing).

INCLUDING CONSTRAINTS gives each regrain copy the parent's NOT VALID CHECK as a validated one, so a pre-existing violating row the table still serves fails every copy batch (23514). F5-03.reason: Reproduces on both trees, but every part of it is documented and intended. pgpm_archive/README.md (Limits) says 'Parquet supports eleven types: int4, int8, float8, boolean, text, timestamp/timestamptz, uuid, json/jsonb, and numeric(p,s)'. date is not on that list, so the encoder raising 'unsupported column type date' is the documented limit, and the claim's own scenario concedes the README documents it. docs/reference.md says pgpm.set_archive_fn checks only the argument list (the regprocedure cast) and the return type, nothing about the columns a given strategy can encode. A date control column is not a special case: any column outside the eleven types (int2, varchar, a composite) behaves the same way. That fails safe by design: nothing is retired unarchived, no rows are lost. A set-time preflight would be an enhancement, not a defect in a documented contract. Not a re-find: #774 bullet 1 is the duplicated type mapping, not this.

The only fault left is that the no-argument failure line is labelled LIVENESS, which is a naming question and not a Tier 5 acceptance of a state the guard should refuse.

The locktrace track's one mutation (maintain_no_commits_trace, mutate.py --list --track=locktrace) only removes maintain_all's commits, and a mutant that does not install is refused by discriminate.sh's installed=0 branch before starved() is asked. A failed attach is therefore the environment's (no privileged container, kernel headers, a probe timeout), and the same job's unmutated run of lock_trace.sh (test.sh run_locktrace, before discriminate.sh --track=locktrace) fails red in such an environment. This is the shape the pass-12 backlog verification struck as B06-01 on #1146: 'no mutant can make one of them its only failure ... they are environment probes the mutant does not touch ... A failure there comes from the environment, which the rubric strikes.' Not known_open: #1146 bullet 1 (unprefixed witnesses, lock_trace.sh among them) is recorded fixed by #1211.

IN SELECT loop target, so an unmarked text local filled with quote_ident output by a FOR loop passes CHECK 1 (valid PL/pgSQL, holds "Foo Bar" at run time), contrary to CLAUDE.md's 'fails CI when a quote-derived text local lacks the suffix'; the docstring's deliberate scope narrows expressions, not assignment forms; distinct from #1236 (strip_noise) and #1031 A1031-3 (initialisers). F8-05.root_cause: bench/run.sh's 4f conservation gate judges 'every history row still present' (its own comment; bench/README.md: 'asserts row conservation (every history row still present after the swap)') by count(*) before vs count(*) where id < MONO_HI after, so a regrain that loses row 5 and invents row 50 in the range is reported conserved (REGRAIN_CONSERVED stays partial/1, never 0); count-for-identity. Not known-open (no open issue names this gate). Rebuilt: the original grepped three exact spellings of run.sh's lines, so any fix that respelled them would fail its LIVENESS and never pass; the rebuild runs run.sh's own section-4 anchor region and whole 4f block against the tree's bench/sql/00_schema.sql and reads the gate's verdict REGRAIN_CONSERVED, with an intact-history control so an always-failing gate cannot pass; confirmed it passes against an identity-checking gate.

F8-06.reason: Reproduces on both trees, but the behaviour is documented and intended, and nothing accepts a state it should refuse. upgrade_in_place.sh's header names it as such: '7. LIVENESS WITNESS: the machine still runs afterwards ... every assertion above it is satisfied by a database that merely sits there.' bench/liveness_witness_labels.sh's FLOOR deliberately holds it as a witness ('upgrade_in_place|W|maintain_obtain\(\) minted nothing after the upgrade', line 209), set beside the one check it holds as a defect check because a mutation exists to fail it (DEGRADE_COLS, #1175). Consequence: none of Tier 5's kind. On an install that breaks post-upgrade obtain, the guard still sets fail=1 and exits nonzero in CI. discriminate.sh's starved() would fail closed, refusing such a mutant as starved rather than certifying anything. No mutation in bench/mutations/ models that defect. The claim is a disagreement over labelling, not a guard passing on broken code.

F8-07.reason: Reproduces on both trees, but it is the documented, deliberate rule. bench/discriminate.sh's comment on starved() says: 'a guard that failed without printing any failure line, or only a restated verdict, is not read as starved (the classifier's rule too)'. #1177 (commit 939bfb83) carved out only the case where the file reached no assertion, because the wrapper then prints 'LIVENESS: the assertions were reached at all' itself. In this case the LIVENESS premise passed, and by the contract (header, #713: a LIVENESS witness 'says the fixture reached the state the defect needs') a failure after it counts as evidence against the code. A raise there cannot be told apart from the mutated function raising under test. Reading it as starved would refuse real catches. classify_claims.py's failure_kind applies the same rule: a psql error is 'defect' whatever premises passed. The sibling bullet A1033-1 on #1033 (a guard that exits non-zero without a failure line is certified) was struck on the same grounds. The 'later fixture statement' in the repro is only the finder's label on a statement placed after the premise.
